evidence.estrutura: Wells used local journalism, civic organization and national campaigns against racial violence; no strong federalism doctrine, though local self-organization mattered.
evidence.representacao: Suffrage and civil-rights activism strongly support equal voting rights and democratic inclusion.
evidence.poder: Her anti-lynching campaign directly opposed extralegal violence and state failure to protect equal rights, placing her strongly on civil-liberties and due-process principles.
evidence.imigracao: Her politics focused racial citizenship more than immigration; equality arguments favor pluralism but border policy remains underdetermined.
evidence.diplomacia: She was not primarily a foreign-policy actor; keep moderate rather than infer militarism from domestic conflict.
evidence.intervencao: No clear foreign-intervention doctrine is established; opposition to domination supports restraint.
evidence.economia: Her reform work addressed racial and economic inequality but did not define a comprehensive ownership system; mildly reformist mixed economy.
evidence.controle: Support for legal enforcement of equal rights implies public regulation, not command economic planning.
evidence.comercio: No substantive trade doctrine is established.
evidence.religiao: Christian reform language was present in her milieu and life, but her public claims were civic and rights-based rather than theocratic.
evidence.moral: Anti-racism, suffrage and women’s rights strongly support egalitarian social positions.
evidence.tecnologia: Investigative journalism and data collection show pragmatic use of modern tools, not a technology ideology.
